Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) is characterized by bilateral fibrocystic changes resulting in pronounced kidney enlargement. Impairment of kidney function is highly variable and widely available prognostic markers are urgently needed as a base for clinical decision-making and future clinical trials. In this observational study we analyzed the longitudinal development of sonographic kidney measurements in a cohort of 456 ARPKD patients from the international registry study ARegPKD. We furthermore evaluated correlations of sonomorphometric findings and functional kidney disease with the aim to describe the natural disease course and to identify potential prognostic markers. Kidney pole-to-pole (PTP) length and estimated total kidney volume (eTKV) increase with growth throughout childhood and adolescence despite individual variability. Height-adjusted PTP length decreases over time, but such a trend cannot be seen for height-adjusted eTKV (haeTKV) where we even observed a slight mean linear increase of 4.5 ml/m per year during childhood and adolescence for the overall cohort. Patients with two null PKHD1 variants had larger first documented haeTKV values than children with missense variants (median (IQR) haeTKV 793 (450–1098) ml/m in Null/null, 403 (260–538) ml/m in Null/mis, 230 (169–357) ml/m in Mis/mis). In the overall cohort, estimated glomerular filtration rate decreases with increasing haeTKV (median (IQR) haeTKV 210 (150–267) ml/m in CKD stage 1, 472 (266–880) ml/m in stage 5 without kidney replacement therapy). Strikingly, there is a clear correlation between haeTKV in the first eighteen months of life and kidney survival in childhood and adolescence with ten-year kidney survival rates ranging from 20% in patients of the highest to 94% in the lowest quartile. Early childhood haeTKV may become an easily obtainable prognostic marker of kidney disease in ARPKD, e.g. for the identification of patients for clinical studies. The classic phenotype involves kidney enlargement due to the development of ubiquitous renal microcysts 1 . There is pronounced clinical variability both for the renal and the hepatic clinical phenotype that can only partially be explained by underlying genetic variants in the main affected gene PKHD1 1 – 3 . Treatment in ARPKD currently remains symptomatic 2 , 4 . This is partly due to the fact that primary endpoints for interventional clinical trials have not yet been established and that risk cohorts have not been defined. For autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) total kidney volume (TKV) and height-adjusted total kidney volume (haTKV) serve as surrogate risk markers of disease progression in adults 5 . For ARPKD a loose inverse correlation between TKV and kidney function has been observed in children and it is widely accepted that kidney growth patterns show differences between ARPKD and ADPKD 6 – 8 . In a sonographic study from 1995 following nine patients with the histological diagnosis of ARPKD, a decrease of kidney size with time was observed in five of the nine subjects 9 . Another study showed stable renal size in 16 ARPKD children surviving the neonatal period 8 . More recently, in two cohorts of 31 and 50 ARPKD patients, respectively, no clear correlation between eGFR slope and kidney size were detected 10 , 11 . Kidney volumes and lengths remained stable over time in one of the cohorts 11 . Overall, however, the natural history of kidney size in ARPKD and its correlation to kidney function remain incompletely understood. Over the past years we have established an international ARPKD cohort study 12 , 13 . Using this observational longitudinal data we have previously identified antenatal sonographic markers as risk markers for early dialysis dependency in ARPKD 14 . In the current study we aimed to (1) characterize in detail the longitudinal courses of different kidney size measures during childhood and adolescence and to (2) evaluate a potential association of early height-adjusted estimated total kidney volume (haeTKV) with kidney survival in ARPKD on the basis of a well-characterized cohort of up to 456 patients. This improved understanding of clinical courses may serve as a base to identify ARPKD patients that are at risk of developing early kidney failure. extracted_data.document_summary: This observational study characterized the longitudinal development of kidney size (length and volume) in pediatric Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) patients. It aimed to evaluate the association of early height-adjusted estimated total kidney volume (haeTKV), particularly measurements within the first 18 months of life, with kidney survival, identifying it as a clear prognostic marker for kidney survival. The study also detailed statistical methodologies for estimating annual eGFR loss and haeTKV increase in children, including those on Kidney Replacement Therapy (KRT).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) progression and kidney development.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Longitudinal sonographic monitoring of kidney measurements (pole-to-pole length and estimated total kidney volume) was performed in a cohort of up to 456 ARPKD patients (up to 1205 datapoints for PTP length from 408 patients and up to 508 datapoints for eTKV from 161 patients) during childhood and adolescence, prior to nephrectomy. A specific focus was placed on height-adjusted estimated total kidney volume (haeTKV) in the first eighteen months of life. Some comparisons with MRI or CT were performed for validation in a small subset. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported as part of this observational study; Kidney Replacement Therapy (KRT) was a condition for some statistical analyses of the cohort.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Volumetric Measurement (sonographic), calculated using ellipsoid formula

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Generally increases or remains stable with a slight increase; higher in more severe genetic variants and advanced CKD stages; inversely correlated with kidney survival.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: During childhood and adolescence, a slight mean linear increase of 4.5 ml/m per year was observed. haeTKV values correlated with PKHD1 genetic variants: Null/null (median 793 ml/m), Null/mis (median 403 ml/m), and Mis/mis (median 230 ml/m). haeTKV increased with CKD stage, ranging from a median of 210 ml/m in stage 1 to 472-632 ml/m in stage 4-5. Higher haeTKVmax18 (>597 ml/m) was associated with significantly lower 10-year KRT-free survival (20% in the highest quartile vs. 94% in the lowest, p < 0.001). Mean annual increase of haeTKV was estimated by a linear regression of haeTKV versus age.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: haeTKV reflects kidney enlargement due to fibrocystic changes, which is a key characteristic of ARPKD and indicative of disease progression and severity. It also functions as a prognostic marker for kidney survival.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) progression, specifically longitudinal changes during childhood and adolescence, initial measurements in the first eighteen months of life, stratified by age, genetic variants, and CKD stage. Also includes longitudinal assessment of haeTKV versus age in children and children undergoing Kidney Replacement Therapy (KRT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the severity and progression of kidney disease in ARPKD. It is a strong potential prognostic marker for kidney survival in childhood and adolescence, particularly when measured in the first 18 months of life (haeTKVmax18), and can identify patients at heightened risk of early kidney failure or progression to KRT for clinical studies.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased with increasing age. The correlation to kidney function was less clear (p = 0.1 for both haAvPTP length and alternative haAvPTP length upper vs. lower quartile) than for haeTKV.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney size and growth in Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment of kidney growth in pediatric ARPKD patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Used to assess kidney growth; showed less prognostic discrimination for kidney function/survival compared to haeTKV.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Kidney function (derived from blood parameters, calculated value)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Calculated measurement based on full age spectrum formula; calculation of kidney filtration capacity.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower (with higher haeTKV); inversely correlated with haeTKV; annual loss observed.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Inverse correlation between haeTKV and eGFR. Mean eGFR at the end of the first year of life was 21 ml/min/1.73 m2 in the highest haeTKVmax18 quartile, 58 ml/min/1.73 m2 in the two middle quartiles, and 101 ml/min/1.73 m2 in the lowest haeTKVmax18 quartile. Annual eGFR loss was estimated for each patient as the slope coefficient of a linear regression of eGFR versus age, normalized as percental yearly change, for patients with at least three visits spanning at least one year.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney function, specifically glomerular filtration capacity, and a key marker of kidney health and disease progression.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Assessed in pediatric ARPKD patients in relation to kidney size (haeTKV) and CKD stage. Also in longitudinal assessment of eGFR-age relationships in children, including those undergoing Kidney Replacement Therapy (KRT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Directly indicates kidney function status; lower eGFR values signify poorer kidney function and are associated with larger early kidney volumes (haeTKVmax18) and thus poorer prognosis in ARPKD. Annual eGFR loss signifies declining kidney function and disease progression.
